chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Marlowe Morris, John Hammond and a pianist who never showed up
summary: Marlowe Morris had a trio at Small's but was irresponsible and later became an alcoholic despite Hammond's help.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: See, while I check that is, if you just switch that on and don't pull that lever down, it doesn't record.
Well, what were you saying about
Oh, John, he had a nice trio and Small's at the bar, had a group upstairs (unintelligible) bandstands.

This was around in '49-'50-'51. Harry Ball had a group upstairs, and he had a good trio, and John Hammond had already set up a record date for him. But you know Marlo was irresponsible too. And when you come down for that date, he don't show. Like when we were down at the Stables I was working with Mr. Page. Mario was on piano. And (unintelligible) be looking around to see if he's coming. He'd come in just in time after we'd played the show. So Lips said, what am I going to do with him? I said, forget about him. Let him come -- I said, what you going to do with him? You know, because he's irresponsible. John tried to get him here about -- I think it was last year or either the first of this year. He's living over in Brooklyn. He's a friend of mine. We all belong to the same lodge. And he got to become a wino.
See? And John Hammond contacted him (unintelligible) tried to help him out in the street straighten him out (unintelligible). Guy come all cockeyed drunk, they tell me. See, that's --
Yeah. I know a friend of mine was recording piano players, and I said, well, maybe Marlowe's around still playing, and he came to that Jazz Museum one day,
and I hadn't seen him for a year or two, and he was so ridiculously drunk, you know, that you couldn't recommend anybody to --
-- that's right. John Hammond (unintelligible) thought a lot of the guy.
And he really wanted to do something for him, but the guy never would show up right. Just happened just recently.
Come to see the man, and he's all lopsided and -- oh, no, but John had been a very good fellow, very fine fellow, very fine.
